news.headline: A Mars Rover Sets a New Driving Record
news.body: NASA's Perseverance rover has now driven farther than any vehicle on another world! On October 11, its trip meter reached about 28 miles (45 kilometers). That might not sound far for a car, but on Mars the rover has to steer around giant boulders and up steep, rocky slopes all by itself. Engineers taught it new tricks, like figuring out exactly where it is by comparing its own photos with pictures taken from space. Its practice twin on Earth even got a Guinness World Records plaque!

news.headline: The World's Biggest Cowboy Hat Lands in Texas
news.body: A racetrack in Austin, Texas, just showed off a cowboy hat sculpture so big it set a world record! The hat is 43 feet wide, 47 feet long, and 17 feet tall. That's taller than a giraffe! A judge from Guinness World Records measured it on Monday and named it the world's largest fiberglass sculpture of a hat. The giant hat was built to celebrate a big Formula 1 car race coming to the track. Good luck finding a cowboy big enough to wear it!

news.headline: Helpers Pack Almost a Million Meals in One Hour
news.body: More than 1,000 volunteers in Des Moines, Iowa, teamed up to pack 990,864 meals in just one hour, a new world record! Working at 60 tables, they filled bags with rice, soy, dried vegetables, and vitamins. Each meal can be cooked with just boiling water. Half of the meals will go to people in Iowa and the rest to communities around the world. Together, they could give about 2,000 children healthy food for a whole year. Teamwork really adds up!

fun_fact: A day on Mars is called a sol, and it lasts about 40 minutes longer than a day on Earth. That's a little extra time to play! 🔴
